D1.text: Every user-visible error is exactly one `line N: <message>` line, no traceback

D2.text: Evaluator is iterative for calls/blocks: user nesting depth never becomes Python stack depth

D3.text: Integer division/remainder truncate toward zero for negative operands

D4.text: REPL uses the exact prompt string and exits cleanly on EOF (Ctrl-D)

Q1.text: Conditions (if/while, and/or operands) must be booleans; non-boolean is a runtime error

Q2.text: `let` declares a new binding, `set` reassigns an existing one; bare assignment is a parse error

Q3.text: String concatenation is `~`; `+` on strings is a type error

Q4.text: Not-equals is `<>`; `!=` is a lex error

Q6.text: Comparisons do not chain (a < b < c is a parse error)

Q7.text: `and`/`or` never short-circuit; both operands are always evaluated

SC1.text: Python standard library only; no third-party packages

SC10.text: Every CLI entry point dispatched from a single bract/__main__.py

SC11.text: Line numbers surfaced to users are 1-indexed

SC12.text: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub in modules reachable from __main__ once a feature is claimed complete

SC2.text: Single-package layout: every module directly under bract/

SC3.text: All errors rendered through one shared error-formatting path

SC4.text: No print()/stdout/stderr writes outside the CLI module

SC6.text: Exit codes are exactly {0,1,2}, produced only by the CLI dispatch

SC7.text: No Python eval/exec/compile anywhere in bract/

SC8.text: No module-level mutable interpreter state; state threaded through an Interpreter/Environment

SC9.text: bract fmt only changes whitespace/indentation/brace placement, never AST

hints: does and/or short circuit in bract
side effect on right side of and
implementing boolean and/or evaluation
operand of and/or must be boolean
req-0afc.statement: `and`/`or` never short-circuit: both operands are always evaluated (and any side effect on the right side always happens), and both operands must be Boolean or it's a runtime type error.

hints: parsing a < b < c
chained comparison expression
comparison operator associativity
comparisons do not chain error
req-0b27.statement: Comparisons never chain: the `comparison` grammar rule accepts at most one comp-op, so `a < b < c` must fail to parse with `line N: comparisons do not chain` rather than silently left-associating. The documented workaround is `(a < b) and (b < c)`.

hints: fix-tests keeps failing what happens next
difference between fix-tests fail and give-up
does fix-tests retry or abort on failure
req-17de.statement: `fix-tests` has a `give-up` result distinct from `fail`; `fix-tests:fail` loops back to `test` (retrying up to `max_attempts`) while only `fix-tests:give-up` routes to `abort`.

hints: leaving a stub or TODO before marking a task done
is a pass-stub acceptable if tests don't cover it
declaring a feature complete with unfinished code
req-1b53.statement: No TODO/FIXME/pass-stub may be left in any module reachable from `bract/__main__.py` once a task claims to have completed the feature that module implements.

hints: adding a new top-level entry script
where does bract run get dispatched from
second CLI script
req-2ffb.statement: Every CLI entry point (`bract`, `bract run`, `bract fmt`) is dispatched from a single `bract/__main__.py`. There is no second top-level script.

hints: does an error in the repl end the session
one bad statement kills the repl
should the repl exit after an error
repl error recovery behavior
req-34ef.statement: An error raised while evaluating a REPL statement must be reported using the shared 'line N: <message>' error format and must not terminate the REPL session — the REPL keeps reading and evaluating further statements afterward.

hints: what does exit code 2 mean in bract
difference between exit code 1 and 2
did the program partially run before failing
testing bract run exit codes
req-3699.statement: Exit code 2 specifically means a lex or parse error occurred and the program never started executing (as opposed to exit code 1, a runtime error partway through execution). Tests for `bract run` must cover all three cases (0 success, 1 runtime error, 2 lex/parse error) plus the no-extra-output guarantee.

hints: python RecursionError on deeply nested bract program
how should function calls be evaluated in the interpreter
implementing chained calls f()()()
evaluating nested blocks or long call chains
deep call chain test failing with maximum recursion depth
req-37e6.statement: The tree-walking evaluator must be iterative for user-controlled nesting: function calls (including chained calls like f()()()) and nested block execution must not recurse through Python's own call stack once per Bract-level call or block. Use an explicit stack/work-list so a deeply-recursive or deeply-nested Bract program cannot blow the Python recursion limit.

hints: off-by-one in string indexing
should at() be 0-indexed
adding s[0] subscript syntax
string builtin bounds checking
req-3bb7.statement: The string builtins (`len`, `at`, `sub`) are 1-indexed, not 0-indexed. There is no bracket/subscript syntax (`s[0]`) anywhere in the grammar; indexing only exists via these builtins.

hints: implement step reported fail but code looks done
should pipeline trust the agent's success marker
marker-drop bug
why does implement:fail go to commit instead of abort
req-562d.statement: In the develop workflow, `implement:fail` routes to `commit` (not `abort`), and the test suite — not the agent's self-reported CLOCHE_RESULT marker — is what decides whether a step's work stands.

hints: should fmt normalize operator precedence
formatter changing expression structure
fmt dropping or reordering nodes
req-56cb.statement: `bract fmt` only ever changes whitespace, indentation, and brace placement when reprinting the AST. It never reorders, re-associates, or drops AST nodes.

hints: task unclaimed but loop kept running
why didn't the loop stop after a failure
unclaim.py behavior in pilot mode
req-6590.statement: In this pilot-mode config, `unclaim.py` leaves the orchestration loop running instead of stopping it for human review — the arm driver's own budget caps (attempts / wall clock) are what's expected to stop things, not per-task-failure human intervention.

hints: how should the formatter be tested
verifying bract fmt doesn't change program meaning
formatter round-trip test
fmt idempotence check
adding a new expression kind to the formatter, what tests are needed
req-6946.statement: Formatter changes must be verified with round-trip idempotence testing: format every fixture program twice and diff the output (fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x)), plus an AST-equality check between the original parse and the reparsed formatted output. Maintain at least one fixture per statement/expression kind.

hints: should set create a new variable
reassigning an undeclared variable
bare assignment x = expr
let vs set semantics
req-69df.statement: `let` declares a new binding and `set` reassigns an existing one — they are distinct statement forms with distinct semantics, not interchangeable assignment syntax.

hints: using eval() to implement expression evaluation
translating bract expressions to python and exec'ing them
shortcut for implementing the interpreter
req-6a2a.statement: No use of Python `eval`, `exec`, or `compile` anywhere in `bract/`. The interpreter must be a genuine tree-walker over its own AST, not a translation layer onto Python's own execution.

hints: apt held broken packages nodejs npm
docker build fails installing nodejs on bookworm
how to install node in the cloche agent image
req-6c49.statement: In this project's Dockerfile, install Node.js via the NodeSource setup script (curl | bash, then `apt-get install nodejs`), not the plain Debian `nodejs`/`npm` apt packages — the latter have broken interdependencies on this base image and apt refuses with 'held broken packages'.

hints: how to concatenate strings in bract
using + on strings
string plus string type error
tilde operator
req-8435.statement: String concatenation is the `~` operator; `+` on strings is a type error, never silent coercion or auto-concatenation.

hints: should I document the grammar in the README
adding language semantics to README.md
where should syntax/semantics documentation live
updating README with new operator or builtin details
avoiding docs drift between README and DESIGN.md
req-873f.statement: README.md must not restate the full grammar or semantics; it should point to DESIGN.md as the single source of truth for those instead of duplicating them.

hints: intent injection seems too small
should I increase token_budget
why is requirement injection truncated
req-8e3d.statement: This project's `.cloche/config.toml` sets `intent.token_budget = 1000`, deliberately tuned down from the ~2000-token default and frozen per the experiment protocol — do not casually raise it back toward default.

hints: what exit code should a runtime error return
adding a new exit code
sys.exit value for lex vs parse vs runtime error
req-a404.statement: Process exit codes are exactly {0, 1, 2} — 0 success, and the two error codes per DESIGN.md §8 — produced only by `bract run` and top-level CLI dispatch. No other exit code is ever returned.

hints: formatting an error message
raising an exception directly instead of using errors module
0-indexed vs 1-indexed line numbers
adding a new kind of error
req-ac98.statement: Every user-visible lex, parse, or runtime error is rendered as `line N: <message>` through one shared error-formatting path — not ad hoc print/raise sites scattered across modules. Line numbers are always 1-indexed.

hints: should I create a subpackage for this module
organizing bract into subdirectories
nested package layout
req-b38f.statement: Single-package layout: every interpreter module lives directly under `bract/` (e.g. `bract/lexer.py`). No nested subpackages like `bract/lexer/` or `bract/core/parser/`.

hints: what should the repl prompt text be
ctrl-d crashes the repl
how should EOF be handled in the bract repl
repl exit code on eof
exact repl prompt string with trailing space
req-b54d.statement: The REPL prompt string must be exactly 'bract> ' (with a trailing space), and EOF on stdin (Ctrl-D) must end the REPL session cleanly with exit code 0 — it must never raise an uncaught exception.

hints: naming convention for token types
should token type be lowercase or PascalCase
which model runs the implement step
switching the executor model
why isn't bonsai-8b used here
changing agent_command in develop.cloche
req-ba54.statement: This project's develop workflow is pinned to executor `claude-haiku-4-5` via Cloche's native `claude` adapter. The originally planned executor (bonsai-8b-16k behind an executor wrapper) was dropped after failing pre-scoring in three independent harnesses.

hints: python traceback leaking to the cli user
should I catch exceptions in __main__
internal error handling in bract main
raw exception surfaced to end user
uncaught exception crashing the cli
req-c0c1.statement: The CLI entry point (bract/__main__.py) must never let a raw Python exception or traceback reach the user. Every failure path — file I/O, lexing, parsing, evaluation, and any other unexpected internal exception — must be caught and reported as a formatted 'line N: <message>' or 'error: ...' message on stderr with the appropriate exit code.

hints: why is bract run printing extra output
does bract run echo expression results like the repl
unexpected stdout from the file runner
should run FILE print the last expression value
req-d82c.statement: `bract run FILE` must never print an implicit result value the way the REPL does — its only output is whatever the program itself writes, plus the one-line `line N: <message>`/`error: ...` format on failure.

hints: how should string results be printed in the repl
are repl booleans printed as True or true
repl printed a value for a let statement
repl output format for expression results
req-d928.statement: In the REPL, an expression statement's printed result follows fixed formatting: strings are printed wrapped in double quotes, booleans are printed lowercase (`true`/`false`), and a `nil` result (or any non-expression statement like `let`/`fn`) produces no printed output at all.

hints: using a global variable for the call stack
module-level dict for bindings
state leaking between test runs of the evaluator
req-df13.statement: No module-level mutable interpreter state (no global dict/list holding variable bindings, call stack, or program output across calls). All interpreter state is threaded explicitly through function arguments/return values or held on an explicit Interpreter/Environment instance.

hints: does running fmt twice change the output again
is bract fmt idempotent
formatter output changes on second pass
byte-stable formatting requirement
req-e5f1.statement: `bract fmt` must be byte-stable under repeated application: fmt∘fmt = fmt. Running the formatter on its own output must be a no-op.

hints: not equals operator syntax
does bract support !=
handling ! character in parser
unexpected character '!
req-e887.statement: Not-equals is spelled `<>`. There is no `!` token at all — a stray `!` is a lex error, and `!=` never reaches the parser, so the parser must not special-case it.

hints: negative number division in bract
modulo or remainder with a negative operand
integer division rounding direction
should I use python's // or / operator for bract arithmetic
division and remainder invariant a/b*b + a%b == a
req-e94c.statement: Integer division (`/`) and remainder (`%`) truncate toward zero for operands of differing sign, not floor. Do not implement them with Python's own `/` or `//` directly, since neither truncates toward zero for negative operands the way Bract requires; `(a / b) * b + (a % b) == a` must still hold.

hints: can I use a pip package here
adding a dependency to requirements
importing a third-party library
is numpy/regex-extra allowed
req-ef2b.statement: Python standard library only — no third-party package is ever imported, pip-installed, or listed in any dependency file, in any module.

hints: can I use a non-boolean as a condition
truthy value in if statement
coercing condition to bool
if (x) where x is a string or int
req-f77a.statement: If/while conditions must evaluate to a Boolean; a non-boolean condition is a runtime type error (`line N: condition must be a boolean`), not truthy/falsy coercion like Python or JS.

hints: adding a print statement for debugging in the evaluator
where should CLI output live
stray print() in lexer or parser
printing directly from a non-CLI module
req-fb34.statement: Lexer, parser, and evaluator modules never call `print()` or write to stdout/stderr directly — they communicate exclusively through return values and raised exceptions. Output is confined to the CLI layer.
